newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Stals says IMF loan could help - paper.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Stals says IMF loan could help - paper.

text.p: A loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) could lift South Africa's low reserves and boost foreign confidence in the country, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said in an interview published on Friday.
"A standby facility from the IMF will help in increasing the foreign reserves to a somewhat higher level," he told the weekly Mail & Guardian.

"In furnishing the financial aid, the fund also normally requires a country to fulfil certain conditions which could require even greater monetary and fiscal discipline and could increase the confidence of non-resident investors in the South African economy."
Stals said it would be up to the government to negotiate an acceptable role for the fund if South Africa was to seek a standby facility.
There have been growing calls from business for South Africa to seek IMF assistance to help it push ahead with foreign exchange control liberalisation.
Economists argue abolition of controls on residents is vital, both to allow the market to determine the true value of the rand and to signal government confidence in the economy.

But the authorities' hands are tied by low official gold and foreign exchange reserves which, despite a slight improvement last month, still remain precarious at 10.28 million rand, equivalent to four weeks import cover.
IMF managing director Michel Camdessus has said that an IMF facility -- which could more than double foreign reserves -- could be used to bolster the capital account during a phase of liberalisation.
But some members of the ruling African National Congress are wary of the stigma attached to IMF aid, following unpopular IMF interventions elsewhere in Africa.
